- What would you recommend as a minimum guaranteed GPU footprint for a production lane that will serve ~25 TPS (average) with p95 latency targets of 300–400ms for 2k token requests?

- Procurement needs an initial term length and preferred billing cadence you typically see for customers of our size.

Can you send an options matrix we can present internally?

Hi Lindsey — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short options matrix (attached) and a recommended ramp that balances cost and operational risk. High level summary below; full numbers and example burn rates are in 20261030-capacity-options-v3.pdf attached.

Option A — Conservative (low commitment)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 8 x A100-equivalent (dedicated lane)
- Use case: small pilot + staging; supports ~8–12 TPS steady, bursts to 20 TPS with caching
- Ramp: activate in 2 tranches (4 GPUs on sign, +4 GPUs at 30 days)
- Fallback: automated model fallback to a 4GB quantized variant + shared-hosted bursting
- Pricing: lowest monthly commitment, higher unit price on burst usage

Option B — Balanced (recommended)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 16 x A100-equivalent
- Use case: production GA for ~25 TPS with margin for KV cache overhead
- Ramp: 8 GPUs at contract start, +8 GPUs at go/no-go (30–45 days)
- Fallback: region-aware routing + model-family fallback; can drop to smaller family with graceful degradation
- Pricing: mid-level commitment discount; includes 1 scheduled canary rollout per month

Option C — Aggressive (throughput-first)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 32 x A100-equivalent
- Use case: heavy throughput, predictable latency at scale, multi-region readiness
- Ramp: 12 GPUs on sign (staging), +10 GPUs at 30d, +10 GPUs at 60d
- Fallback: immediate burst capacity from Dedicated reserve pool; cross-region replication available
- Pricing: best unit economics for 12–36 month terms

Other notes:
- Activation lead times: we can stage a small lane (2–4 GPUs) within 7–10 business days for testing; full activation of committed pools typically takes 2–6 weeks depending on inventory and region.
- Pilot: we can do a 60‑day pilot on Option A that credits to the committed term if they convert.
- SLA & billing: monthly billing; preferred contract lengths 12 or 24 months; we can include a 30–90 day ramp credit structure to reduce near-term cash impact.

I've also outlined fallback policies (automated model family fallback, per-route throttles, and a pre-agreed capacity burst budget) in the attachment. If this looks good, I can turn it into a formal SOW and pricing worksheet for procurement.

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick bullets:

- Pricing (12‑month term)
  - Option A (8 GPUs committed): $27,500 / month commit + $0.24 / token-equivalent burst rate
  - Option B (16 GPUs committed): $50,000 / month commit + $0.18 / token-equivalent burst rate
  - Option C (32 GPUs committed): $92,000 / month commit + $0.12 / token-equivalent burst rate

- Pilot credit structure
  - 60‑day pilot on Option A: we can provide a 50% credit of the pilot fees if they convert to Option B within 45 days of pilot end. Avoid fully refundable pilots; conversion credit aligns incentives.

- Buffer & burst approach
  - Recommend a 20% buffer above expected steady-state for Option B (i.e., size to 20% above avg TPS to protect p95s). Provide 200 GPU-hours/month of burst credit included in the mid-tier package; additional burst billed at the burst rate above.

- Activation/inventory notes (fyi for Karthik)
  - For us‑west region we typically have inventory to stage up to 16 GPUs within 10–14 business days; larger activations (≥32) may take 4–6 weeks depending on procurement timelines and GPU procurement cycles.
